question: Which of the following is the main tissue that transports water in a plant from its roots to its leaves?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Xylem**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Xylem is one of the two types of transport tissue in vascular plants.
 
• The basic function of the xylem is to transport water from roots to stems and leaves, it also transports nutrients.
 
• The word xylem is derived from the Greek word xylon meaning wood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Name**
 **Details**
 
 

 Collenchyma
 
 
 
• Collenchyma is a supporting tissue composed of more or less elongated living cells with unevenly thickened non-lignified primary walls.
 
 
 
 

 Parenchyma
 
 
 
• The cellular tissue is typically soft and succulent found in the softer part of leaves, the pulp of fruits.
 
 
 
 

 Phloem
 
 
 
• Phloem is the vascular tissue that transports carbon from leaves to the basal parts of the plant.
